name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
summary: A glute-focused hip extension done with your upper back on a bench or sofa and a dumbbell resting on your hips. It is one of the easiest ways to load the glutes at home.
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back (just below the shoulder blades) against a stable bench or the edge of a sofa. Make sure it cannot slide.
Roll a dumbbell onto your hip crease and hold it with both hands. Pad it with a towel if it is uncomfortable.
Place your feet hip-width apart, flat on the floor, with knees bent so the shins are roughly vertical at the top.
Tuck your chin slightly and keep your eyes forward.
execution: Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
At the top your ribs stay down and your shins are about vertical.
Pause for a moment, then lower your hips under control until they nearly touch the floor.
Repeat without bouncing off the floor.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top: tuck the ribs down and stop when hips and shoulders line up.
Feet too far forward or too close: adjust so the shins are vertical at the top and you feel it in the glutes, not the hamstrings or quads.
Bench or sofa sliding: push it against a wall or use a heavy piece of furniture.
Rushing with momentum: lower slowly and pause at the top of each rep.
